tells.1: The 'a date on the calendar, never as a way of leaving the room' contrast is neat but slightly abstract and engineered. Trimming also drops 'the usual things,' which flattens the emotional beat.
tells.2: The clipped fragment opener and the split ending ('I was ready to go. I just took my time...') can read like deliberate staccato for effect. Otherwise mostly none.
tells.3: The polished 'found myself doing the usual things:' colon-plus-tricolon, the balanced semicolon sentences, the filler 'actually', and typographic curly quotes give it a smooth, template-like finish.
tells.4: It keeps the same colon-introduced tricolon and semicolon symmetry as version 3, plus 'actually' as filler. The prose is evenly polished, with little texture.

reason: Version 2 has the most distinct voice ('caught myself,' 'chewed over the whole drive home') and its rhythm feels like real reflection rather than balanced, polished prose. Versions 3 and 4 are near-identical and read as smoothed. Version 1 is clean but loses some warmth.
